turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. I have twenty minutes, so start with who decided that and when.
"Get this over with." Okay. I asked you a question, Hale: who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Look, your son cheated. Everyone knows it. I'm not wasting my evening on this.

My child never lies, and "everyone knows" is not evidence. If you have something, put it in front of me in writing, or I'm walking up to the principal's office the minute we're done. I'm writing down that you said that.
You lawyers think you can bully anyone.
I'm asking you to follow your own procedure, Hale. Section 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish anything, so tell me what else you have, or this goes upstairs today.
Are you going to keep wasting my time?
I'm not leaving. Show me something with Owen's name and a date on it, or the next conversation I have is with your principal.
